answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The pearl of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Each submission hangs on the ripple of a task receipt, and the cipher is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter.
